To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the online environment of Think.com, with its social software features, can support communities of practice in research partnerships, and that the social software features of Think.com, such as the ‘wall’ and ‘groups’, are essential to the usability of the environment.

(i) communities of practice can be supported through the online environment of Think.com; (ii) online environments can be used to connect stakeholders across Australia and internationally; and (iii) the online environment is a useful tool for facilitating communities of practice in educational research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality and relevance of educational research, and the ways in which online environments might be used to facilitate communities of practice in research partnerships.
the quality of research partnerships, and how online communities of practice can contribute to this quality.

• the development of online communities of practice for educational researchers and practitioners • the development of a model for online communities of practice that is relevant for the Australian education system • the development of an online environment that supports the model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the online communities of practice supported the development of research partnerships and provided opportunities for stakeholders to participate in the research agenda.
the online environment is a useful adjunct to the development of communities of practice, but is no substitute for face-to-face communication.
the communities of practice model is a promising one for the development of research partnerships, and that online communities can be effective in this regard.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for the development of online communities of practice, and have demonstrated that this model can be applied successfully to a range of research partnerships.

we have found that the online environment has been an important tool to connect people, to facilitate the sharing of information, to provide a space for discussion and debate, and to support the development of communities of practice.
we have found that communities of practice supported online can be effective in bringing together diverse stakeholders in the research and knowledge building process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
online communities of practice are a powerful way to bring together stakeholders and facilitate dialogue about educational research.
communities of practice supported with online environments can help to achieve a more equitable research process and more relevant research outcomes.
the online environment is a useful and powerful tool for supporting communities of practice in research.
